newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall St record drives Euro stocks to peaks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall St record drives Euro stocks to peaks.

text.p: European shares made strong gains on Friday morning inspired by Wall Street's rampant bullishness which has driven it to five straight record closes.
New York's latest surge was prompted by surprisingly weak economic data that eased concerns about rising interest rates.
London shares were up 0.6 percent, while French and German shares were up 1.1 and one percent respectively by midmorning. All three made new trading records on the way up.
"This is Nirvana," Phil Orlando, U.S. based chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management, said of Wall Street's rise.
The Dow Jones industrial average surged 135.64 points to 7,711.47, its fifth record in a row. The index closed above 7,500 for the first time only on Tuesday, and ended at 7,575.83 on Wednesday.
"We'll take our cue now from Wall Street -- at least until this afternoon," one Frankfurt share trader said.

U.S. analysts said the American data, which included a surprising decline in U.S. retail sales over the last three months and a higher-than-expected level of weekly jobless claims, proved the country's economic growth remains within the Federal Reserve's -- and therefore the market's -- comfort zone.
Share traders on both sides of the Atlantic concluded there was less danger that interest rates would rise to choke off inflation -- good news for the share prices.
In London, the FTSE 100 advanced further into record ground and was up 28.8 points at 4,786.2 at 1100 gmt.
"If inflation is not picking up, these markets can be re-rated further," one London share trader said. "It's all liquidity driven."
German shares also surged to a record high of 3,751.26, helped by the dollar as well as Wall Street, though they then fell back a touch and stood at 3,748.07, up 40.08, at 1100 gmt.

Other factors pushing the market higher were abating fears about the future of European monetary union as France and Germany appeared ready to reach a compromise on a stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline after the start of the new currency in January 1999.

"There is more and more confidence out there that the euro will come on time, even if it's weaker than expected, so people now expect that money will keep coming into Europe after currency union," a trader said.

In Paris, the blue chip CAC share index rose to a trading high of 2,805.37 points, propelled by Wall Street and hopes of a ratification of a European stability pact at next week's EU Amsterdam summit, traders said. The CAC-40 index was up 31.03 points at 2,791.30 at 1100 GMT.
"There's a lot of volume out there," a broker said. He added that the message from the markets was that "in France, politics don't matter".

Elsewhere, Madrid's IBEX-35 index stood at 6,689.57 points, up 0.25 percent mid-morning, off record high of 6,743.33 points. Swiss shares also hit a record at 5,396.5 points, with the SMI index up 14.9 points at 5,379.1, and Dutch shares advanced to a high of 848.29 points early on, before settling back to 843.21 points, up 3.85.

Meanwhile, the dollar took a breather after a week of wild swings, with traders looking for a cue from a summit of European Union countries starting on Monday and a Group of Seven leading industrial nations meeting later in the week.

U.S.-Japan relations came under the spotlight this week as traders drove the dollar down to a six-month low against the yen on Wednesday amid concern about trade friction between the two and then pushed it back up four percent in the next trading session as such worries ebbed.
They are now looking to next week's G7 summit in Denver for reassurance that trade tensions will remain at bay.

Dollar/mark has acted as a weathervane for hopes of an accord on a EU budget stability pact. Speculation that European economic and monetary union may be delayed was triggered after France on Monday asked for time to consider the pact and urged the adoption of measures to promote growth and employment.

EU officials dispelled such talk, saying the pact will be formally adopted at their Amsterdam summit Monday and Tuesday. This has dislodged the mark from the highs it set early in the week against other European and major currencies.
"People don't want to take any positions ahead of the EU and G7 summits," said Craig Justham, at Creditanstalt Bankverein.
Dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7300 at midday, while dollar/yen was at 114.40.

Expectations grew that the U.S. will refrain from criticising a recent widening in Japan's trade surpluses at the G7 summit after U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Thursday that leaders will not pay special attention to U.S.-Japan trade flows.
Also, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said America will not use the dollar as an excessive instrument of trade policy.
Traders are now looking to May U.S. producer price data at 1230 GMT for clues to whether the Fed will raise rates in July. CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7300 marks and 114.40 yen compared with 1.7265 marks and 113.99 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished was up 28.8 points at 4,786.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed was up 31.03 points at 2,791.30.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 40.08 points at 3,748.07.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1100 GMT
Gold was fixed at $341.20 in early European trade compared with $342.65 an ounce in late trade on Thursday.
